stories.title: Michigan bill would force data centers to disclose water use
stories.dek: A new state proposal requires operators to report how much water their facilities consume. Michigan residents near proposed sites worry about strain on aquifers and municipal supplies already stretched by growth. The measure aims to give communities data before projects get approved.
stories.source_title: Michigan Bill Targets Data Center Water Disclosure - Environment+Energy Leader

stories.title: Lansing weighs tax breaks and power rules for new data centers
stories.dek: Michigan lawmakers are reviewing multiple bills that would change how data centers pay taxes and secure electricity. The proposals could speed up or slow down projects that need hundreds of megawatts. Residents across the state may see higher utility bills or new local revenue depending on what passes.
stories.source_title: Michigan legislators consider a variety of proposals, many bad, on data centers - Mackinac Center

stories.title: Ypsilanti Township Pauses Major Electrical Infrastructure Projects Amid Data Center Concerns
stories.dek: The township board approved a 180-day moratorium on new or expanded high-voltage utility facilities to study impacts from a proposed University of Michigan research computing center backed by Los Alamos National Laboratory.

stories.title: Washtenaw leaders pitch new data center as economic win for county
stories.dek: Officials in Washtenaw County are highlighting jobs and tax revenue from a fresh data center proposal while residents question the power and water demands. The project would add significant load to the regional grid already strained by AI growth. Taxpayers within driving distance will ultimately pay for any utility upgrades needed to support it.
stories.source_title: Leaders Tout New Data Center Project In Washtenaw County Iga świątek (UaqolHuAjQ) - Mshale

stories.title: St. Joseph County weighs noise rules as data centers eye the grid
stories.dek: St. Joseph County is drafting a noise ordinance aimed at data centers that could run 24/7. Officials are also tracking how much extra power these facilities would pull from the regional grid. Residents within 30 miles worry about constant hum and higher electric rates if big loads come online.
stories.source_title: The Data Center Debate: St. Joseph County's Noise Ordinance and Possible Energy Grid Impact - WNDU

stories.title: Campbell coal plant stays open to feed data-center power hunger
stories.dek: The U.S. Department of Energy ordered the J.H. Campbell plant in Ottawa County to keep running, citing rising electricity demand from data centers. Keeping the aging coal unit online means continued emissions and higher costs for ratepayers in western Michigan. The move underscores how AI growth is reshaping the state's energy grid.
stories.source_title: DOE issues sixth order keeping J.H. Campbell plant open - AOL.com

stories.title: Wixom may lift data-center freeze months early
stories.dek: Wixom leaders are weighing whether to end the town's data-center moratorium ahead of schedule. Residents could soon face decisions on large power-hungry projects that affect local electric rates and land use. The move would reopen the door for proposals that have already sparked pushback in Oakland County suburbs.
stories.source_title: Wixom council considers early ending for data-center moratorium - MLive.com

stories.title: New Buffalo blocks storage yard tied to data center project
stories.dek: The township board rejected the permit for a storage facility directly supporting a data center. Residents in Berrien County now face fewer construction impacts and truck traffic near their homes. The decision shows local pushback against supporting infrastructure for these facilities.
stories.source_title: New Buffalo Township board denies permit for storage yard linked to data center - WNDU

stories.title: Michigan's new tax breaks shield data centers from most local property taxes
stories.dek: The state quietly broadened data-center tax incentives, letting operators avoid paying property taxes on equipment and buildings for up to 12 years in many communities. Big Rapids and other rural counties could lose millions in revenue while still bearing higher electricity and water costs. The change rewards companies that locate here but gives townships little leverage to negotiate better deals.
stories.source_title: Michigan expanded data center tax breaks. Here’s what they actually cover - Big Rapids Pioneer

stories.title: Raeden sues Michigan, says moratorium illegally killed Gibraltar project
stories.dek: Data-center developer Raeden is suing the state, claiming Michigan's moratorium on new facilities unlawfully blocked its $500 million Gibraltar campus. The lawsuit could force the state to compensate the company or lift restrictions that have frozen several projects in Wayne County. Local officials and residents who opposed the site now face renewed legal uncertainty over who controls future development.
stories.source_title: Raeden claims Michigan moratorium unlawfully stopped its Gibraltar data center development - Data Center Dynamics

stories.title: Data Center Backlash Spurs Recall Bids Against 28 Michigan Officials
stories.dek: Only one official reaches the November ballot after most petitions failed, as residents vent frustration over projects they feel powerless to stop.

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
